subject: Post-call: Cost qualification & commitment framework for CrystalPay
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chu <alex@crystalpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — cost anchors, ops levers, and next asks

Alex — thanks for the 30 mins earlier. Quick recap while it's fresh and to lock in the asks + handoffs. TL;DR: clear product fit for payments NLP; primary blocker is predictable unit economics and procurement visibility into 3-year TCO.

Key pain points we heard
- High token spend variability across peak flows and reconciliation jobs; CFO wants a bounded forecast.
- Sizing and latency tradeoffs for two workloads: (A) real-time auth/chat (~350M tokens/day peak) and (B) overnight reconciliation batch (~4B tokens/day).
- Internal procurement needs an ops/rollback plan and a clear SLA/discount ask for committed capacity.

Goals you outlined
- Get a 3-year total cost projection for both flows (baseline + two optimization scenarios).
- Surface concrete levers (batching, prefix KV caching, quantization tiering) with estimated token reductions and latency impact.
- Provide a simple commitment framework (monthly reserved vs burst for peak windows) that procurement can approve.

Our proposed approach (next deliverables)
1) TCO workbook (attached) — three scenarios: Baseline (no ops changes), Ops-Optimized (batching + caching), and Aggressive (quantization + reserved pools). Each sheet has 12/36-month views, unit economics per 1M tokens, and sensitivity to peak variance.
2) Mutual action plan (attached pdf) — recommended milestones: pilot (30d), sizing window, SLA terms, and procurement signoff checklist.
3) Quick engineering playbook — small config changes you can try in dev for immediate ~15–30% token reduction (we'll share one-pagers on batching params).

Open questions for you/Procurement
- Target ROI threshold for vendor engagements (e.g., payback in <=9 months?).
- Any internal constraints around encryption/KMS we should model for Private deployment?
- Procurement contact for contract redlines — cc'd?

Immediate asks
- Can you confirm procurement contact and whether CrystalPay prefers annual or quarterly billing for reserved capacity?
- If the baseline numbers in the attached sheet are off materially, send the event counts for auth + reconciliation for May and Jun (CSV) and we'll re-run.

I can turn this into a one-page ROI memo for your CFO tomorrow. Marissa is on copy and will own the TCO workbook updates.

Thanks again — Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0143

Attachment: CrystalPay-TCO-3yr-scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Alex Chu <alex@crystalpay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@crystalpay.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — cost anchors, ops levers, and next asks

Rishi — solid writeup, thanks. A few quick notes from our side:

- Procurement: that's me looped with procurement@crystalpay.com. For initial approvals they'd like a 36-month view and a clear break-even vs current infra spend. I'll flag that CFO wants a 2-way sensitivity (higher-than-expected token growth).
- ROI bar: target payback <= 12 months to move into reserved capacity; we can stretch to 18 months if SLA + data controls are strong.
- KMS: we use our cloud KMS (no HSM). If Private deploy requires HSM, that will complicate timelines — prefer hosted or VPC for now.
Can you: (1) update the TCO sheet with a 36-month tab and a column modeling +25% token growth/year? (2) add an ops-optimized scenario that assumes 40% reduction on the overnight reconciliation workload via batching + KV caching and shows latency changes?
We'll also need a short note describing cancellation/rollback behavior for committed pools in case we exceed token forecasts.
Two next items from us: procurement will send a short checklist; and I can schedule a follow-up call early next week to review the 36-month view.

Appreciate it — Alex
Head of Product, CrystalPay
alex@crystalpay.com | +1 (212) 555-0199
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chu <alex@crystalpay.com>, Procurement <procurement@crystalpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 23 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — cost anchors, ops levers, and next asks

Thanks Alex — noted. We'll: (A) add a 36-month tab with +25%/year sensitivity, (B) model a reconciliations ops-optimized row with conservative 40% token reductions (and call out the assumptions), and (C) add a short cancellation/rollback paragraph for committed pools (grace period, overage billing, automatic fallback to hosted variants).

I'll get Marissa to update the workbook by Monday EOW and share a one-page CFO memo. Also sharing the mutual action plan with suggested timeline and a lightweight SOW template (DocuSign link below) for an initial pilot commitment. If procurement is happy, we can convert the pilot into reserved capacity after the 30-day sizing window.

Proposed 30-min review: Mon 25 Jun, 10:00–10:30 PT — tell me if that works and I'll send a calendar invite.

DocuSign (pilot SOW): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-123
Cheers — Rishi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
